summary: Traces were silently going nowhere. Nothing had reached Langfuse or Jaeger for about thirteen hours, while Nora ran normally and answered messages.
details: Nora builds its own tracing setup so it can keep its rule about which traces are worth recording, and hands that setup to the agent library. The library keeps it but does not switch it on globally — it only does that when it builds one itself. So nothing was ever switched on, and every trace Nora opened quietly went into a stub that records nothing.

Nothing complained, because a stub that records nothing is a perfectly well-behaved stub. The collector was healthy, the address resolved, a test message to it succeeded, and the guard around the setup never fired. Everything reported success because nothing had been asked to do anything.
One line switches it on. Verified against the running system before and after: with it, a test trace reached the store within seconds.

A test now checks that it is switched on. Every existing test in that file called the setup and then asserted nothing at all, which is exactly why this survived them — 'it did not crash' is true of something that does nothing.
limitations: Traces from the silent window are gone. They were never recorded anywhere, so nothing can be recovered.
This does not change which traces are kept. Traces with no model call in them are still dropped on the way to the language-model store by design, and still reach the infrastructure store.
